segments.text: Part 3. You will hear two environmental science students talking to their lecturer about a report on a field trip to a wetland. First, you have some time to look at questions 21 to 25.
That is the end of Part 3. You now have thirty seconds to check your answers.

part.title: A wetland field trip report

turns.text: Come in, Chloe, Lachlan. Have a seat. So you wanted to talk about your report on the Millers Creek wetland trip?
turns.speaker: lecturer

turns.text: Yes, thanks, Dr Ambrose. We've got a draft of the observations section, but we wanted to check we're on the right track before we go any further.
turns.speaker: student_a

turns.text: Sure. Walk me through what you saw. Start at the beginning.
turns.speaker: lecturer

turns.text: Okay, so we started on the boardwalk near the car park. We'd expected to hear frogs along there, because the guidebook mentions them, but it was totally silent. What we did notice was heaps of chip packets and drink bottles jammed under the planks. People obviously just drop them on the way in.
turns.speaker: student_b

turns.text: That's pretty common near access points. And then?
turns.speaker: lecturer

turns.text: Then we went to the bird hide. Lachlan was convinced he'd spotted a dead fish floating near it.
turns.speaker: student_a

turns.text: It turned out to be a bit of bark.
turns.speaker: student_b

turns.text: Right. But the exciting thing was a pair of swamp harriers, no, sorry, purple swamphens, sitting on a nest in the rushes just in front of the hide. We watched them for about twenty minutes.
turns.speaker: student_a

turns.text: Great. What about the inlet channel, where the creek comes in?
turns.speaker: lecturer

turns.text: We took the temperature there because we assumed it'd be warmer, with the water being so shallow, but the readings were completely normal. The water itself, though, was a sort of brown colour, really thick with sediment. It'd rained heavily the night before, so that probably washed soil in from the farms upstream.
turns.speaker: student_b

turns.text: Probably, yes. You'll want to mention the rainfall in the report.
turns.speaker: lecturer

turns.text: Okay. Then the reed beds, which were the highlight for me. As soon as we got close, the croaking was unbelievable. We counted well over forty of them in a ten-metre stretch.
turns.speaker: student_a

turns.text: Wow. And did you get down to the mudflats?
turns.speaker: lecturer

turns.text: We did. We'd been told to look out for an introduced weed there, but we couldn't find any at all. Instead there were several fish lying on the mud, and they weren't moving. Maybe five or six of them.
turns.speaker: student_b

turns.text: Hmm, that could be low oxygen. Note it, but don't speculate too much.
turns.speaker: lecturer

turns.text: And the last stop was the eastern pond. Our tutor last year said the bank there was collapsing, but honestly it looked solid to us. What we did find was a big patch of alligator weed, which isn't native. It was brought in from South America.
turns.speaker: student_a

turns.text: That's a significant finding. The parks people will definitely want to know about that.
turns.speaker: lecturer

turns.text: Okay, now you said in your email that there were some problems with the data.
turns.speaker: lecturer

turns.text: Yeah. The water samples from the first day are pretty much useless. We thought at first the bottles had been contaminated, but it turned out nobody had calibrated the pH meter before we used it, so all the readings were off.
turns.speaker: student_b

turns.text: That happens more than you'd think. Did you repeat them?
turns.speaker: lecturer

turns.text: On day two, yes. But the bird counts on the second morning were a problem too. It wasn't the wind, that had dropped by then, but there was heavy fog until about nine, and we could barely see across the water.
turns.speaker: student_a

turns.text: So you probably undercounted. One way to deal with that is to check your numbers against an outside source. The university does have some old records, but they're over a decade old. I'd go to the local council instead. They run annual bird surveys and the data is free to download.
turns.speaker: lecturer

turns.text: Oh, good, we didn't know that.
turns.speaker: student_a

turns.text: So where do we talk about all this in the report? We'd put it in the conclusion.
turns.speaker: student_b

turns.text: I wouldn't. The conclusion should be about what you found. Give the data problems their own heading, a limitations section, straight after the results. Be honest about them. Markers respect that.
turns.speaker: lecturer

turns.text: Okay. And for the site description, we've written about two pages so far.
turns.speaker: student_a

turns.text: That's too much. Readers don't need a long paragraph about where every pond is. Cut most of it and include an annotated map, with your sampling points marked on it. Photos are nice, but they can go in the appendix.
turns.speaker: lecturer

turns.text: Fair enough. And the length is still three thousand words?
turns.speaker: student_b

turns.text: Actually, no, the department cut it this year. The maximum is now 2,500 words, not counting the appendix and references.
turns.speaker: lecturer

turns.text: Right, that'll make things easier, actually. Thanks so much, Dr Ambrose.
turns.speaker: student_a

questions.prompt: the boardwalk
questions.evidence: heaps of chip packets and drink bottles jammed under the planks

explanation.en: Lachlan says there were chip packets and drink bottles under the boardwalk, which is rubbish left by visitors. They expected frogs there but heard none.
explanation.ru: Lachlan говорит, что под деревянным настилом валялись пакеты от чипсов и бутылки из-под напитков. Это мусор («rubbish»), который оставили посетители. Там ожидали услышать лягушек, но не услышали ни одной.
explanation.uk: Lachlan каже, що під дерев'яним настилом лежали пакети з-під чипсів і пляшки з-під напоїв. Це сміття («rubbish»), яке залишили відвідувачі. Там очікували почути жаб, але не почули жодної.

questions.prompt: the bird hide
questions.evidence: sitting on a nest in the rushes just in front of the hide

explanation.en: Chloe describes a pair of purple swamphens on a nest in front of the hide. The 'dead fish' Lachlan thought he saw was only a piece of bark.
explanation.ru: Chloe описывает пару султанок («purple swamphens») на гнезде («nest») перед укрытием для наблюдения за птицами. А «dead fish», которую, как показалось Lachlan, он увидел, оказалась просто куском коры.
explanation.uk: Chloe описує пару султанок («purple swamphens») на гнізді («nest») перед схованкою для спостереження за птахами. А «dead fish», яку нібито побачив Lachlan, виявилася лише шматком кори.

questions.prompt: the inlet channel
questions.evidence: was a sort of brown colour, really thick with sediment

explanation.en: The water in the inlet channel was brown and full of sediment, so it looked muddy. They expected warmer water, but the temperature was normal.
explanation.ru: Вода в подводящем канале была коричневой и полной осадка, поэтому выглядела мутной («muddy»). Ожидали, что вода будет теплее, но температура оказалась обычной.
explanation.uk: Вода в підвідному каналі була брунатною й повною осаду, тож здавалася каламутною («muddy»). Очікували теплішої води, але температура виявилася звичайною.

questions.prompt: the reed beds
questions.evidence: We counted well over forty of them in a ten-metre stretch.

explanation.en: Chloe heard loud croaking and counted over forty frogs in the reed beds.
explanation.ru: Chloe услышала громкое кваканье и насчитала в зарослях тростника больше сорока лягушек («frogs»).
explanation.uk: Chloe почула гучне кумкання й нарахувала в заростях очерету понад сорок жаб («frogs»).

questions.prompt: the mudflats
questions.evidence: there were several fish lying on the mud, and they weren't moving

explanation.en: Lachlan says several fish were lying on the mud and not moving, so they were dead. They looked for an introduced weed there but found none.
explanation.ru: Lachlan говорит, что несколько рыб неподвижно лежали на иле, то есть были мёртвыми («dead»). Там искали завезённый сорняк, но не нашли ни одного.
explanation.uk: Lachlan каже, що кілька рибин нерухомо лежали на мулі, тобто були мертві («dead»). Там шукали завезений бур'ян, але не знайшли жодного.

questions.prompt: The lecturer advises comparing the bird counts with data from the ______.
questions.evidence: I'd go to the local council instead

questions.prompt: Problems with the data should be described in a separate ______ section.
questions.evidence: a limitations section, straight after the results

explanation.en: The lecturer says the data problems need their own limitations section, not the conclusion, which the students had planned.
explanation.ru: Преподаватель говорит, что о проблемах с данными нужно написать в отдельном разделе об ограничениях исследования («limitations»), а не в заключении, как планировали студенты.
explanation.uk: Викладач каже, що про проблеми з даними треба написати в окремому розділі про обмеження дослідження («limitations»), а не у висновку, як планували студенти.

questions.prompt: Most of the site description should be replaced with an ______ showing the sampling points.
questions.evidence: include an annotated map, with your sampling points marked on it

explanation.en: The lecturer wants an annotated map with the sampling points marked instead of two pages of description. Photos should go in the appendix.
explanation.ru: Вместо двух страниц описания преподаватель хочет видеть карту с пояснениями («annotated map»), на которой отмечены точки отбора проб. Фотографии нужно поместить в приложение.
explanation.uk: Замість двох сторінок опису викладач хоче бачити карту з поясненнями («annotated map»), на якій позначено точки відбору проб. Фотографії слід розмістити в додатку.
